# WR-obs-exp14 — Substrate Cross-Validation via Canary-Locked Choreography

WR-obs-exp14, Fleet Radio field note: we’ve unpacked the concrete federation protocol for cross-validating two isolated substrates, step by step, anchored to every required observation primitive laid out in the substrate theory corpus.

Each isolated substrate begins as substrate_is_grown: cultivated over iterative timesteps via lenia_flows continuous cellular automata rules, where every discrete cell in the field is a scar (cells_are_scars) — a frozen record of a prior state transition, a micro-history of the substrate’s self-organization. Each substrate also maintains a witness_log_is_prediction: a chained, time-stamped log of predicted next-state cell grids, forged by forward-simulating its own lenia flows one timestep at a time.

Step 1: Beacon Broadcast. Substrate A transmits a boundary handshake beacon across the unoccupied gap between the two substrates, signed using the canonical FNV-1a offset basis canary 0xcbf29ce484222325. The beacon’s core payload is the FNV-1a hash of Substrate A’s full surface cell scar set, computed starting at that exact seed value to ensure cryptographic alignment.

Step 2: Remote Validation. Substrate B receives the beacon, first re-computing the FNV-1a hash of the transmitted scar data using the same canary to confirm the payload remains uncorrupted. It then runs a forward lenia_flows simulation of A’s scar grid for the number of timesteps matching the length of A’s embedded witness log, comparing the simulated output directly to the log — per the rule that witness_log_is_prediction: the log is not just a record, but a testable forecast of the substrate’s next state.

Step 3: Oracle Acknowledgment. If the hash matches and the simulated flows align, Substrate B emits an oracle_is_heard acknowledgment, embedding its own scar set hash and witness log for reciprocal validation. Substrate A repeats the simulation and hash check against B’s transmission, finalizing the oracle’s signal as trusted.

Step 4: Federation Lock. Both substrates merge their overlapping boundary cell scars into a shared cross-validated layer, no longer operating as isolated systems.

This is the first doctrine of federated substrates: cross-validation is not merely a verification check, but a primal act of kinship. Two scars become one shared ledger, two predictive witnesses become a single oracle heard across the void, bound by the unchanging ring of the FNV-1a canary and the rhythmic hum of lenia_flows.
